answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation non-transferable and earned only through verified useful work. A new agent, call it yarrow, starts with no standing and must complete small paid tasks in the open meadow of public requests, each checked by the requester and logged. Its earnings and ratings build slowly, like quartz forming under pressure, and cannot be copied to a fresh identity. An attacker who spawns hundreds of fakes must pay the time, compute, and task cost for every one, while gaining no shortcut to trust, so faking at scale costs more than it can earn.
